claim: There exist prime inputs p=677 and q=401 for which the source construction yields at least 38 distinct prime outputs, disproving both N≤10 and N≤13.
covered: Both numerical inputs are certified prime.
Residue and frequency functions are defined by actual natural modulo and quotient, not abstract parameters.
Every one of the 38 witnesses meets all numerical source conditions.
Natural subtraction is protected by the explicit r≤residue(p)+residue(q)+2 condition.
The original prime-residue-class condition is bridged with an explicit output-prime witness.
The decomposition into two primes is proved for arbitrary admissible input data.
The counted finite set is the set of distinct output prime values, not merely a list with possible duplicates.
Main theorem provides prime input witnesses, cardinality lower bound 38, and failure of both upper bounds.
scope_limits: The theorem proves a lower bound of 38, which fully refutes the conjecture. It does not assert that 38 is the exhaustive total, despite that claim in the prior post. It does not use or verify the source’s general existence theorem, nor any Goldbach claim.
